metadata.title: Simplifying Ratios and Dividing in a Ratio
metadata.vcaa_description: Use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving ratios, rates and scale, including map scales and unit conversions.
metadata.target_mastery: Simplify ratios involving whole numbers, fractions, decimals, and mixed metric units, divide a quantity in a given ratio, and use map scales.
prerequisites: Highest Common Factor (Section 1D) and Lowest Common Multiple
Metric conversions for length, mass, capacity, and time

key_vocabulary.definition: A comparison of two or more quantities measured in the same units, written in a specific order using a colon.
A ratio $a : b$ where $a$ and $b$ are whole numbers with no common factor greater than $1$ ($\text{HCF}(a, b) = 1$).
A ratio $1 : n$ comparing a drawing or map length to the corresponding real-world length in the same units.

theory.title: Simplifying Ratios (Whole Numbers, Decimals, Fractions, and Mixed Units)
theory.explanation: A ratio compares quantities of the same kind and has no units in its simplified form. If the quantities have different units (such as centimetres and metres), first convert both to the smaller unit. To simplify a whole-number ratio $a : b$, divide both parts by $\text{HCF}(a, b)$. For decimal ratios, multiply by a power of $10$ first; for fraction ratios, multiply both parts by the Lowest Common Denominator.
theory.callout_title: Convert to the Smaller Unit First
theory.callout_rule: When simplifying $45\text{ minutes} : 2\text{ hours}$, convert $2\text{ hours}$ into $120\text{ minutes}$ first ($45 : 120 = 3 : 8$) so you work entirely with whole numbers.

theory.title: Dividing a Quantity in a Given Ratio (Unitary / Total-Parts Method)
theory.explanation: To divide a total quantity $Q$ in the ratio $a : b$, first add the parts to find the total number of parts ($a + b$). One part equals $\frac{Q}{a+b}$, so the two shares are $\frac{a}{a+b} \times Q$ and $\frac{b}{a+b} \times Q$.
theory.callout_rule: Always check that your calculated shares add up to the original total quantity $Q$!

theory.title: Map Scales and Scale Drawings
theory.explanation: A map scale written as $1 : k$ means $1\text{ unit}$ on the map represents $k$ of the exact same units in real life. To find the real-world distance, multiply the map distance by $k$ and convert to larger practical units (such as metres or kilometres). To find the map distance, divide the real-world distance by $k$.
theory.formula_latex: \text{Actual Length} = k \times \text{Map Length}, \quad 1\text{ km} = 1000\text{ m} = 100\,000\text{ cm}
theory.callout_rule: Since $1\text{ m} = 100\text{ cm}$ and $1\text{ km} = 1000\text{ m}$, there are $100 \times 1000 = 100\,000\text{ cm}$ in $1\text{ km}$ (five zeros).

worked_examples.title: Simplifying Ratios with Mixed Units and Fractions
worked_examples.problem: Simplify the following ratios to simplest whole-number form: (a) $600\text{ m} : 2.4\text{ km}$ and (b) $\dfrac{3}{4} : \dfrac{5}{6}$.

steps.thinking: In part (a), convert $2.4\text{ km}$ to metres ($2.4 \times 1000 = 2400\text{ m}$) so both parts have the same unit, then divide by $\text{HCF}(600, 2400) = 600$.
In part (b), multiply both fractions by $\text{LCD}(4, 6) = 12$ to clear the denominators.

now_you_try.hint: Convert $2\text{ hours}$ to $120\text{ minutes}$ in (a), and multiply by $\text{LCD}(3, 5) = 15$ in (b).

worked_examples.title: Dividing a Quantity in a Three-Part Ratio
worked_examples.problem: Concrete for a driveway in Werribee is mixed using cement, sand, and gravel in the ratio $1 : 2 : 5$ by mass. How many kilograms of each material are required to make $400\text{ kg}$ of dry concrete mix?

steps.thinking: Add the ratio parts to find the total number of parts: $1 + 2 + 5 = 8$ parts.
Multiply each ratio part by $50\text{ kg}$ and check that the three masses sum to $400\text{ kg}$.

worked_examples.final_answer: $50\text{ kg}$ cement, $100\text{ kg}$ sand, and $250\text{ kg}$ gravel

now_you_try.problem: Three business partners in Bendigo share a profit of $\$18\,000$ in the ratio $2 : 3 : 4$. Find the largest share.
now_you_try.hint: Total parts $= 2 + 3 + 4 = 9$. The largest share is $4$ parts.

worked_examples.title: Using Map Scales in Victorian National Parks
worked_examples.problem: A bushwalking map of Wilsons Promontory National Park has a scale of $1 : 50\,000$. Two campsites are $7.2\text{ cm}$ apart on the map. Find the actual ground distance between the campsites in kilometres.

steps.thinking: Multiply the map distance ($7.2\text{ cm}$) by the scale factor $50\,000$ to find the actual distance in centimetres.
Convert centimetres to kilometres by dividing by $100\,000$ ($100\text{ cm/m} \times 1000\text{ m/km}$).

now_you_try.problem: On a Grampians walking map with a scale of $1 : 25\,000$, a trail measures $14\text{ cm}$. What is the actual length of the trail in kilometres?

common_misconceptions.title: Simplifying a Ratio Without Converting to the Same Unit First
common_misconceptions.misconception: Simplifying $20\text{ cm} : 2\text{ m}$ as $10 : 1$ by dividing $20$ and $2$ without converting metres to centimetres.
common_misconceptions.correct_concept: Both quantities must be expressed in the same unit before comparing. Since $2\text{ m} = 200\text{ cm}$, the ratio is $20\text{ cm} : 200\text{ cm} = 1 : 10$.
common_misconceptions.counter_example: $20\text{ cm}$ is one-tenth of $2\text{ m}$, not ten times longer than $2\text{ m}$!

common_misconceptions.title: Dividing the Total Quantity by One Ratio Part Instead of the Sum of Parts
common_misconceptions.misconception: When dividing $\$60$ in the ratio $2 : 3$, dividing $60 \div 2 = 30$ and $60 \div 3 = 20$.
common_misconceptions.correct_concept: A ratio $2 : 3$ has $2 + 3 = 5$ equal parts in total, so $1$ part is $60 \div 5 = \$12$. The shares are $2 \times 12 = \$24$ and $3 \times 12 = \$36$.
common_misconceptions.counter_example: In $2 : 3$, the second share must be larger than the first share, whereas $60 \div 3 = 20$ is smaller than $30$.

fluency_and_understanding.question: Simplify the ratio $56 : 84$.
step_by_step_solution: Find $\text{HCF}(56, 84) = 28$.
Divide both parts by $28$: $56 \div 28 : 84 \div 28 = 2 : 3$.

fluency_and_understanding.question: Simplify $1.8 : 0.45$ to simplest whole-number form.
step_by_step_solution: Multiply both parts by $100$ to clear decimals: $180 : 45$.

fluency_and_understanding.question: Simplify $750\text{ g} : 3\text{ kg}$.
step_by_step_solution: Convert $3\text{ kg}$ to grams: $3000\text{ g}$.
Simplify $750 : 3000$ by dividing by $750$: $1 : 4$.

fluency_and_understanding.question: Divide $\$540$ in the ratio $4 : 5$.
step_by_step_solution: Total parts $= 4 + 5 = 9$. One part $= 540 \div 9 = \$60$.
Shares are $4 \times 60 = \$240$ and $5 \times 60 = \$300$.

fluency_and_understanding.question: Find $x$ if $5 : 8 = 35 : x$.
step_by_step_solution: The first term is multiplied by $35 \div 5 = 7$.
Multiply the second term by $7$: $x = 8 \times 7 = 56$.

fluency_and_understanding.question: In a cordial mix of syrup and water in the ratio $2 : 7$, there is $630\text{ mL}$ of water. How much syrup is in the mix, and what is the total volume of cordial?
step_by_step_solution: $7$ parts of water $= 630\text{ mL}$, so $1$ part $= 630 \div 7 = 90\text{ mL}$.
Syrup ($2$ parts) $= 2 \times 90 = 180\text{ mL}$.
Total cordial ($9$ parts) $= 9 \times 90 = 810\text{ mL}$.

problem_solving_and_modelling.question: The interior angles of a triangle are in the ratio $3 : 4 : 5$. Find the size of each angle in degrees.
step_by_step_solution: The angle sum of a triangle is $180^\circ$, and total parts $= 3 + 4 + 5 = 12$.
One part $= 180^\circ \div 12 = 15^\circ$.
The three angles are $3 \times 15^\circ = 45^\circ$, $4 \times 15^\circ = 60^\circ$, and $5 \times 15^\circ = 75^\circ$.

problem_solving_and_modelling.question: An architectural blueprint for a new community library in Geelong uses a scale of $1 : 200$. The main reading hall is $28\text{ m}$ long and $16\text{ m}$ wide in real life. Find the length and width of the reading hall on the blueprint in centimetres.
step_by_step_solution: Convert real-life dimensions to centimetres: $28\text{ m} = 2800\text{ cm}$ and $16\text{ m} = 1600\text{ cm}$.
Divide each by the scale factor $200$: Length $= 2800 \div 200 = 14\text{ cm}$ and Width $= 1600 \div 200 = 8\text{ cm}$.

problem_solving_and_modelling.question: Two Stroke Engine fuel for a lawnmower requires petrol and oil mixed in the ratio $25 : 1$. How many millilitres of oil must be added to $6.5\text{ L}$ of petrol?
step_by_step_solution: Convert $6.5\text{ L}$ of petrol to millilitres: $6.5 \times 1000 = 6500\text{ mL}$.
Since $25$ parts $= 6500\text{ mL}$, $1$ part of oil $= 6500 \div 25 = 260\text{ mL}$.

reasoning_and_communication.question: If $a : b = 2 : 3$ and $b : c = 4 : 5$, find the combined three-term ratio $a : b : c$ in simplest whole-number form. Explain your method.
step_by_step_solution: The common term $b$ has value $3$ in the first ratio and $4$ in the second ratio.
Scale both ratios so that $b$ equals $\text{LCM}(3, 4) = 12$: multiply $2 : 3$ by $4$ to get $8 : 12$, and multiply $4 : 5$ by $3$ to get $12 : 15$.
Combine the two linked ratios into $a : b : c = 8 : 12 : 15$.

reasoning_and_communication.question: A map has a linear scale of $1 : 10\,000$. Explain why $1\text{ cm}^2$ on this map represents an actual area of $10\,000\text{ m}^2$ ($1\text{ hectare}$) rather than $10\,000\text{ cm}^2$.
reasoning_and_communication.final_answer: $1\text{ cm}$ on the map represents $10\,000\text{ cm} = 100\text{ m}$, so a $1\text{ cm} \times 1\text{ cm}$ square represents $100\text{ m} \times 100\text{ m} = 10\,000\text{ m}^2$
step_by_step_solution: A $1\text{ cm}$ side on the map corresponds to $10\,000\text{ cm} = 100\text{ m}$ in real life.

Therefore, a square of $1\text{ cm} \times 1\text{ cm}$ on the map corresponds to a real square of $100\text{ m} \times 100\text{ m} = 10\,000\text{ m}^2$ (which equals $10^8\text{ cm}^2$, the square of the linear scale factor).

reasoning_and_communication.question: In a bag of red and blue marbles, the ratio of red to blue marbles is $3 : 5$. When $12$ more red marbles are added to the bag, the new ratio of red to blue marbles becomes $7 : 5$. Find the original number of red and blue marbles in the bag.
step_by_step_solution: Notice that the number of blue marbles ($5$ parts) did not change, while the red marbles increased from $3$ parts to $7$ parts.
The increase of $7 - 3 = 4$ parts equals the $12$ added red marbles, so $1$ part $= 12 \div 4 = 3$ marbles.
Originally there were $3 \times 3 = 9$ red marbles and $5 \times 3 = 15$ blue marbles.
